definition: A nonelected invention is the invention that is not selected by the filer of a patent application when several inventions are impermissibly claimed, as only one may be selected for final evaluation. See: 37 CFR § 1.141 The patent application filer may be asked to restrict their application to a single invention if multiple are claimed. The selected invention is the elected invention, while other inventions are the nonelected inventions. A rejoinder is the process of withdrawing the restriction requirement between an elected invention and a non-elected invention when all claims to a non-elected invention depend on, or otherwise require, all of the limitations of an allowable claim.
